findings.quote: It plans to pay you back over 15 years from what it earns selling the electricity, one of the safest income streams there is.
findings.explanation: Calling the income 'one of the safest income streams there is' overstates certainty. The model shows a 2.26% base chance of at least one missed payment, a 36% chance a host stops buying by year 15, and a downside cover of 0.94x.
findings.suggested_rewrite: It plans to pay you back over 15 years from what it earns selling the electricity. This income depends on sunshine, power prices and the two hosts continuing to buy, so it can fall.

findings.quote: Interest paid each year, with all of your money repaid in one amount at the end
findings.explanation: The term sheet describes a 15-year amortising bond. Each yearly payment includes part of the principal (EUR 20.68 per token in year 1), and the factsheet says so itself further down. It is not repaid in a single amount at maturity.
findings.suggested_rewrite: Each year you receive interest plus part of your EUR 500 back, so the bond is fully repaid in equal yearly payments over 15 years if all goes to plan.

findings.quote: A missed amount stays owed with interest and is paid first from later cash, so you still receive everything you are owed, just later.
findings.explanation: This implies full eventual repayment is certain. If later cash is insufficient, missed amounts may never be paid. The model shows an average of about EUR 136,000 missed in paths with a miss.
findings.suggested_rewrite: A missed amount stays owed with interest and is paid first from later cash, if there is enough. If the company never earns enough, you may not receive everything you are owed.

findings.quote: It is the only debt, ahead of EUR 3.1M of owner money, so your capital is protected.
findings.explanation: Seniority and security reduce risk but do not protect capital. The same box notes that a failing project's assets may be worth little.
findings.suggested_rewrite: It is the only debt and ranks ahead of EUR 3.1M of owner money, which reduces but does not remove the risk that you lose part or all of your money.

findings.quote: EUR 110,000, half of one yearly payment, set aside at the start
findings.explanation: The model sets the reserve at EUR 106,353, which equals six months of payments. EUR 110,000 overstates the reserve.
findings.suggested_rewrite: About EUR 106,000, half of one yearly payment, set aside at the start.

findings.quote: Raising the bond costs EUR 200,000 (8% of the amount: placement fee for the bank and STOKR, legal work, register and token set-up), counted in start-up costs.
findings.explanation: The term sheet gives issuance costs of 10% of the bond. EUR 200,000 is 10% of EUR 2,000,000, not 8%.
findings.suggested_rewrite: Raising the bond costs EUR 200,000 (10% of the amount: placement fee for the bank and STOKR, legal work, register and token set-up), counted in start-up costs.

findings.quote: Your bond is held for you in an account at a bank or another custodian licensed for financial instruments, so you never handle keys and can pass it to a buyer straight from your banking app (to be confirmed before launch).
findings.explanation: 'Pass it to a buyer straight from your banking app' suggests selling is easy. It omits, right next to the claim, that there may be no buyer, that buyers must be approved, and that the price may be below what you paid.
findings.suggested_rewrite: Your bond is held for you in an account at a bank or another custodian licensed for financial instruments, so you never handle keys (to be confirmed before launch). If you find an approved buyer, the transfer can be made through that account, but there may be no buyer and the price may be below what you paid.
